subject: Collection rails & trace-code guidance for ApexPay — EUR/GBP settlement and intermediary fees

Ben —

Attaching this month's collection file and invoice: the payments we collected Nov 30–Dec 10 were split across EUR and GBP rails. Our bank has started applying variable correspondent bank charges on the EUR->USD sweep and a fixed intermediary fee on the GBP CHAPS -> USD settlement. Two quick asks:
1) Is Redwood able to accept net-of-fees (i.e., beneficiary receives whatever lands after intermediaries) and still reconcile to the invoice? If yes, what remittance/tracking fields do you need so we can attach the right trace code?
2) If Redwood requires gross receipts, can you confirm the preferred wire instruction fields (OUR/SHA/BEN) and whether Redwood will absorb/intervene on correspondent fees or prefer us to re-invoice?

Invoice attached (ApexPay_invoice_DEC2026.pdf). Also attaching a capture from our bank showing the SWIFT path (swift_snapshot.txt).

Thanks — trying to close month cleanly.

Carlos Ruiz

Carlos —

Thanks for the attachments and the clear summary. Looping in our Finance leads (Laura) and Tax (Neha) to confirm the accounting/VAT angle. A few practical items from our side so we can reconcile quickly:

High-level options we use depending on commercial terms:
- Option A (preferred by Redwood): Paid amount must arrive NET to our account (beneficiary receives the invoice amount). Customer/ordering bank should set the SWIFT charge type to OUR (ordering bank pays all fees), or ensure the remitter pays correspondent charges up front. If the instructing bank sets SHA, the intermediary fees will typically be deducted mid-route and the beneficiary will receive less.
- Option B: If funds arrive short (SHA/BEN path), we accept net receipts but we will need a per-payment remittance that includes the payer reference and the exact intermediary deduction amount so we can short-pay apply and either invoice the shortfall or offset on a later invoice.

To reconcile automatically please ask your bank to include the following in outgoing transfers (these are the minimum we require):
- Field: Remittance Info / End-to-end reference ("TRN:") -> e.g., TRN:APX-INV-20261201-<payerref>
- Field: Sender to Receiver Information (SWIFT 72) -> add "REDWOOD-TRACE:<invoice#>"
- In the payment advice XML: include the exact intermediary charge element if a SHA flow is used.

Sample collecting accounts we can use (placeholders — please confirm with Treasury before instructing):
- EUR collection (SEPA preferred when payer is EU): IBAN: DE35REWD00001234567890 | BIC: REWDDEFFXXX | Beneficiary: Redwood Inference EU Limited
- GBP collection (CHAPS/FT): Sort Code: 60-12-34 | Acc: 12345678 | Beneficiary: Redwood Inference UK Ltd

If you choose Option A (ordering bank pays): please request your bank to set the charge type to OUR. Note that not all payer banks will support OUR for SEPA or domestic rails; in those cases we fall back to Option B and ask for detailed remittance metadata.

Also: if you prefer us to "gross-up" (we absorb intermediary fees and increase invoice to cover them), that requires sales approval; we can accommodate as a one-off for onboarding/expansion deals.

Can you confirm which rails were used per payment and provide two example payment messages (one EUR, one GBP) from your bank? That will let us map the intermediary nodes.

Best,
Ben Carter
Manager, Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

Carlos —

Following Ben's note — a few treasury/ops clarifications and the practical reconciliation path we'd use:

1) Preferred model for multi-currency collections
- We prefer single-currency collecting accounts (one per currency). That keeps FX exposure separate and makes VAT treatment clearer.
- For EUR: SEPA where possible to avoid intermediary banks. If you cannot route SEPA, please include the correspondent chain so we can identify deductions.

2) Intermediary / correspondent fees
- If the payment arrives short (SHA/BEN), Redwood will accept and will create a short-payment memo against the invoice. Our default is to re-invoice the shortfall on the next monthly invoice unless a written exception is approved by Revenue Ops.
- Occasionally Sales will approve absorbtion of fees for strategic customers — please flag if this is a renewal/expansion scenario.

3) Traceability requirements (minimum)
- Beneficiary account name exactly as on file for reconciliation
- Full remittance text with: invoice number(s), payer reference, and TRN/END2END ID
- A CSV from your bank showing gross amount, intermediary fees and net landed amount is ideal for automated matching.

4) Example wire instruction block you can give to your payers/banks:
-----BEGIN INSTRUCTION-----
Ordering bank: Please mark charges as OUR if you can so beneficiary receives full invoice amount.
Remittance: TRN:APX-INV-20261201-<payerref> | Invoice: #APX-2026-12-01 | Beneficiary: Redwood Inference EU Limited
EUR Account (SEPA preferred): IBAN DE35REWD00001234567890 | BIC REWDDEFFXXX
If SEPA is not possible (non-EU payer): use correspondent bank path and include itemized intermediary charges in the payment advice.
-----END INSTRUCTION-----

5) Next steps from ApexPay
- Please send one sample RAW payment message for an EUR and a GBP movement (SWIFT MT103/ISO20022 XML). Those samples let Treasury map correspondent nodes and estimate typical intermediary deductions.

Happy to coordinate a 30 min call if your ops team wants to walk through the samples together.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Treasury & Billing | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Carlos —

Quick VAT and policy answers from Tax:

1) VAT reverse-charge
- Redwood will issue EU invoices with standard reverse-charge wording if the buyer provides a valid EU VAT registration number. Please collect and pass the buyer's VAT ID to us at billing@redwood.ai so we can include it on the invoice.
- If the buyer is not VAT-registered, VAT rules depend on the country of the buyer; consult us if you see local VAT applied by payers.

2) Intermediary fee handling — policy practicals
- We accept net receipts (SHA/BEN) provided ApexPay supplies the bank detail CSV + MT103s so we can map deductions and auto-apply short payments.
- For small fixed intermediary fees (GBP CHAPS $15–25), Redwood will tolerate these as net deductions for standard customers and will not automatically re-invoice small variances under $25 per item; larger or systematic short-pays will be re-invoiced.
- If you want Redwood to absorb fees consistently, Finance requires a written SOW addendum or approval from Sales to amend invoicing terms.

3) Practical checklist for ApexPay ops
- Send MT103s / ISO20022 XML for the two sample payments (EUR + GBP).
- Provide CSV with: payer_name, payer_bank, gross_amount, intermediary_fees_total, net_received, payment_date, trace_ref
- If possible, ask your collecting bank to include the end-to-end ID in the ISO payment info element to speed up reconciliation.

We can handle reconciliation on our side once the sample files are in. If you want, we'll run the first month in "net-accept" mode and surface any exceptions for manual review; that tends to be the fastest path.

Thanks — and happy holidays.

Neha Kapoor
Tax Counsel | Redwood Inference
